text:
Alex Newhook has 10 points in 20 games, including two two-goal nights, against Dallas and in the 4-2 win in Toronto. With Ivan Demidov out, he's on Montreal's top line beside Juraj Slafkovsky and Oliver Kapanen, which is a bigger job than the Canadiens drew up for him.

The goals are fair, 5 on 4.6 expected. The problem is everything else at five on five. Montreal takes only 38% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Newhook on the ice, almost 18 points worse than without him, the biggest gap on the team. Our model notes chances against pile up with him on, and Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 9% of forwards for creating offense last season. That's a hard profile for a top-line role.

He brings real things: speed, a clean breakout (59% of exits with possession by Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking), and a Stanley Cup ring from Colorado in 2022. Our talent range has him around 47 points. Watch his five-on-five numbers as long as he's on the first line, because that's where the Habs' results are running ahead of their play.
